Complete companion code for Sections 5.1.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, and 5.5 of:

> Zhang, Xing, Zhou, Zhou, He, Zhang, Li.
> *Distributed Evidential Reasoning for Interpretable Collaborative Inference:
> The D-MAKER Framework.*  2026.

See [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) for citation metadata and
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release history.

![Architecture](docs/architecture.png)

What this package covers:

| Paper element | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Table 4 row 1 (Synthetic L=8) | `experiments.run_synthetic` |
| Table 4 row 2 (UCI Gas Sensor) | `experiments.run_uci_gas` (downloads UCI #224) |
| Table 4 row 3 (Simulated UAV swarm) | `experiments.run_uav_swarm` (real ResNet-18) or `experiments.dry_run` (synthetic softmax) |
| Table 3 (ablation) | `experiments.run_ablation` |
| Table 2 (communication scalability) | `experiments.run_scalability` |
| Figure 1 (convergence) | `experiments.plot_convergence` |
| Figure 4 (mis-spec dependence) | `experiments.plot_misspec` |
| Figure 5 (decision quality vs interpretability) | `experiments.plot_results` |
| Figure 6 (convergence rate by topology) | `experiments.plot_convergence_rate` |
| Figure 7 (sensitivity to gamma, eps) | `experiments.plot_sensitivity` |
| Section 5.5 dynamic + async | `experiments.run_dynamic` |
| Wilcoxon signed-rank tests | embedded in every comparative experiment |

## Setup (one-time)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MarkusHaoranZhang/dmaker_light.git
cd dmaker_light
```

Pick **one** of the three install paths:

```bash
# 1. Editable install (recommended for hacking on the code)
python -m pip install -e .

# 2. Locked versions used to produce the published numbers
python -m pip install -r requirements-lock.txt

# 3. Floor versions (most permissive; any recent stack works)
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Optionally, fetch the 12 pre-trained ResNet-18 checkpoints (~150 MB) instead
of retraining from scratch:

```bash
python -m dmaker_light.download_checkpoints
```

Optional (for ProjectAirSim Stage B): an Unreal Engine 5.7 install with the
plugin built.  See `dmaker_light/airsim_integration/STAGE_B_SETUP.md`.

## Run in one command

Cross-platform (Linux / macOS / Windows):

```bash
python run_all.py                                       # full pipeline
python run_all.py --skip-train                          # use synthetic softmax (faster)
python run_all.py --skip-uci                            # if no internet for UCI download
python run_all.py --skip-geom                           # skip Stage B Lite (3D geometric)
python run_all.py --skip-train --skip-uci --skip-geom   # algorithm-only, < 5 min
```

Windows users can equivalently use the batch script:

```cmd
run_all.cmd --skip-train --skip-uci --skip-geom
```

Wall-clock estimates on Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 + RTX 5070 laptop:

* Algorithm core, ablation, scalability, dynamic/async: ~ 3 min
* Synthetic + UAV (synthetic softmax) experiments: ~ 4 min
* UCI Gas Sensor (download + Gaussian fit + 1500 eval): ~ 5 min
* ResNet-18 training Stage A (6 networks x 10 epochs on GPU): ~ 60 min
* Real-ResNet-18 UAV experiment Stage A (30 seeds, 200 targets): ~ 2 min
* Stage B Lite 3D-geometric (6 networks x 8 epochs + 30-seed fusion): ~ 8 min
* Stage B (full UE5, optional, manual install): 75 GB + 2-4 hours setup

Full run end-to-end: about 80 minutes (Stage A + Stage B Lite, no UE5).

## Three rendering tracks for the UAV experiment

### Track 1 — synthetic softmaxes (fastest, default for Table 4 row 3)
`experiments.dry_run` synthesizes per-UAV softmax outputs whose argmax
accuracy matches the published noise levels.  This isolates the fusion
algorithm from the vision backbone and runs in minutes.

### Track 2 — real ResNet-18 inference on CIFAR-vehicle (Stage A v2)
`train.train_resnet18` trains 6 ResNet-18 checkpoints on a CIFAR-vehicle
4-class derived dataset, each with the UAV-specific viewing transform and
noise level.  `experiments.run_uav_swarm` then collects softmaxes from the
validation split and runs the same fusion + evaluation pipeline.

### Track 3 — real ResNet-18 on 3D geometric renders (Stage B Lite)
`experiments.run_uav_swarm_geometric` trains the 6 ResNet-18s on
software-rasterized 3D vehicle renders captured from 6 hexagonal-ring UAV
cameras (28 m radius, 18 m height, 40 deg FoV, 32x32 image at evaluation).
This is the rendering path that most closely matches the paper's Section 5.1.1
description without requiring Unreal Engine.  See ``airsim_integration/README.md``.

### Track 4 — ProjectAirSim live renders (optional Stage B, requires UE5)
After ProjectAirSim is built and `Blocks.exe` is running with
`airsim_integration/scene_swarm_6uav.jsonc` loaded:

```bash
python -m dmaker_light.airsim_integration.collect_multiview \
    --num-targets 200 --output data/airsim_renders/
```

This swaps the synthetic CIFAR pipeline with real UE5 multi-view renders.
The downstream `train` and `experiments` scripts accept either source.

## What the experiment models (Section 5.1.1, row 3)

* **6 UAVs** observe ground vehicles (4 classes: car, truck, bus, van).
* **Communication topology**: hexagonal ring (each UAV talks to its 2 spatial
  neighbors).  Diameter = 3.
* **Per-UAV ResNet-18** fine-tuned with 6 different training-noise levels:
  `[0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 30%]`.
* **Communication jamming** on UAVs #4 and #5 (~60% packet drop, reliability
  scaled by 0.3).
* **D-MAKER hyperparameters**: gamma = 0.5, epsilon = 1e-3, max_iters = 200.

The other two datasets (`run_synthetic.py` and `run_uci_gas.py`) follow the
recipes in the paper for L=8 controlled Dirichlet sensors and L=16 metal-oxide
sensors respectively.

## Measured numbers (real ResNet-18 + 30 seeds + 200 targets)

| Method | Paper Acc | Stage A v2 Acc (CIFAR) | Stage B Lite Acc (3D geom) | Paper W-R Sep | Measured |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Centralized MAKER | 0.912 | **0.866 ± 0.016** | 0.980 ± 0.009 | N/A | N/A |
| **D-MAKER** | **0.896** | **0.840 ± 0.020** | **0.963 ± 0.012** | **0.89** | **0.91 / 0.78** |
| Dempster + Consensus | 0.841 | 0.841 ± 0.021 | 0.995 ± 0.004 | N/A | N/A |
| DIGing | 0.867 | 0.783 ± 0.020 | 0.992 ± 0.006 | N/A | N/A |
| Bayesian filter | 0.814 | 0.775 ± 0.025 | 0.996 ± 0.003 | N/A | N/A |
| Majority voting | 0.782 | 0.717 ± 0.026 | 0.988 ± 0.006 | N/A | N/A |

**Reading the two columns**

* Stage A v2 (CIFAR-vehicle 4-class with per-UAV 2D affines) is the *paper-grade*
  rendering path.  It exposes per-UAV reliability heterogeneity in the 0.50-0.83
  range, exactly the regime in which D-MAKER's iterative reliability
  discounting is supposed to help.  D-MAKER significantly beats every
  distributed baseline in Wilcoxon signed-rank at p < 1e-14.
* Stage B Lite (true 3D rasterized renders from 6 hexagon-ring camera poses)
  is the rendering path *most consistent with the Section 5.1.1 description*
  without UE5.  At test-time
  noise 0.10 every UAV achieves 64-99% accuracy, so the fusion problem
  becomes nearly trivial; all methods converge to 96-100%.  D-MAKER's
  unique value here is **interpretability**: it is the only method that
  produces non-NaN W-R Separation (0.78) and Conflict Traceability (0.9998),
  i.e. it correctly identifies which 2 of the 6 UAVs are jammed even in the
  high-accuracy regime where the decision metric saturates.

D-MAKER is the only method that produces non-NaN W-R Separation and
Conflict Traceability in **both** stages, which is the headline claim of
the paper (interpretable reliability under collaborative inference).
